Here's the handoff, ready to paste:

```
ON-CALL HANDOFF — Gateway 503s

ROOT CAUSE
Deploy dep-4471 (gateway, a.novak, "config: connection-per-request
for pool isolation") landed at 2026-03-14T02:13:41Z as config
generation 119. It flipped gateway.pool.perRequest from false to
true. That change made requests stop sharing pooled connections;
each one grabbed its own. The pool is capped at 20 connections and
was overrun within 33 seconds.

First warning:  2026-03-14T02:14:14.920Z — connection acquire took
                100ms (normal is single-digit ms)
First failure:  2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z — req-07401, /v1/cart,
                503 after 659ms
                ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED (size 20, in_use 20, waiting 13)

Errors are still active as of the last log line, 2026-03-14T03:59:27.974Z
(size 20, in_use 20, waiting 74). Wait queue and error latency have
both grown steadily, so this has not self-recovered.

IMPACT WINDOW
Started:  2026-03-14 02:14:18 UTC
Ongoing:  through at least 2026-03-14 03:59:27 UTC (end of captured
          log — assume still live until confirmed otherwise)
Duration so far: at least 1 hour 45 minutes

Affected routes: /v1/cart, /v1/session, /v1/checkout, /v1/orders,
/v1/catalog/search — all failing with 503 across every upstream
(billing-svc, orders-svc, catalog-svc, accounts-svc).
Not affected: /health (steady 200s), worker.log shows all 4 job
replicas running clean the whole window — this is gateway-only.

ROLLBACK
Roll back dep-4471 on the gateway service. Revert
gateway.pool.perRequest to false (or raise the pool size well past
20 if per-request connections are wanted long-term). No other
deploy in that window touches the gateway — the next one,
dep-4472 (billing-svc, 02:41 UTC), is unrelated and shipped after
the incident started.
```

That's the whole handoff, done and ready to hand off.
